questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Each coxal bone of the pelvic girdle is formed by the fusion of three bones. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.explanation:
Each coxal bone forms by the fusion of the ilium, ischium and pubis.
The acetabulum lies at the point where these three bones fuse.
The sacrum is a fused vertebra of the vertebral column. It belongs to the axial skeleton, not to the coxal bone.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following joints in increasing order of the movement they allow:
P. Joint between the parietal bones of the cranium
Q. Joint between two adjacent lumbar vertebrae
R. Joint between the humerus and the pectoral girdle
questions.explanation:
P: The cranial bones are joined by sutures, which are fibrous joints and allow no movement.
Q: Adjacent vertebrae form a cartilaginous joint, which allows limited movement.
R: The humerus and pectoral girdle form a synovial ball and socket joint, which allows considerable movement.
So the increasing order is P < Q < R.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The human skull is described as dicondylic because:
options: It is made of two sets of bones, cranial and facial
It articulates with the vertebral column through two occipital condyles
The lower jaw articulates with the skull at two points
Each middle ear has two condyles for attaching the ear ossicles
questions.explanation:
The skull articulates with the superior region of the vertebral column by two occipital condyles.
This is why it is called a dicondylic skull.
The condyles articulate with the first vertebra, the atlas.
Option (1) is a true fact about the skull, but it does not explain the term 'dicondylic'.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Cardiac muscles are striated in appearance yet are involuntary.
Reason (R): The activities of cardiac muscles are not directly controlled by the nervous system.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Cardiac muscle is striated in appearance but works involuntarily.
R is true. NCERT says cardiac muscle is involuntary because the nervous system does not control its activity directly.
R therefore explains the involuntary nature described in A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The 8th, 9th and 10th pairs of ribs are called vertebrochondral (false) ribs.
Reason (R): These ribs do not articulate directly with the sternum but join the seventh rib with the help of hyaline cartilage.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The 8th to 10th rib pairs are termed vertebrochondral or false ribs.
R is true. Ventrally, these ribs join the seventh rib through hyaline cartilage instead of reaching the sternum directly.
This indirect connection to the sternum is exactly why they are called false ribs, so R explains A.
By contrast, the 11th and 12th pairs have no ventral connection at all and are called floating ribs.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
A. Fascia
B. Sarcolemma
C. Sarcoplasm
D. Sarcoplasmic reticulum
List-II
(i) Store house of calcium ions
(ii) Plasma membrane lining a muscle fibre
(iii) Collagenous connective tissue layer holding fascicles together
(iv) Content of the muscle fibre containing many nuclei
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation:
A-(iii): Fascia is the common collagenous layer that binds the fascicles together.
B-(ii): Sarcolemma is the plasma membrane of the muscle fibre.
C-(iv): Sarcoplasm is enclosed by the sarcolemma and has many nuclei.
D-(i): Sarcoplasmic reticulum is the store house of Ca++.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The cross arms seen on a polymerised myosin filament are formed by the light meromyosin portions projecting outwards.
Statement II: The head and short arm of each meromyosin project outwards at regular distances and angles from the surface of the myosin filament.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. The cross arm is the HMM component (head plus short arm), not LMM. The LMM tails form the body of the polymerised filament.
Statement II is correct. NCERT states that the HMM projects outwards at regular distances and angles from the filament surface. This projection is called the cross arm.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Both arthritis and gout involve inflammation of joints.
Statement II: In gout, joint inflammation results from the deposition of calcium salts lost from bones.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
Statement I is true. NCERT defines arthritis as inflammation of joints and gout as inflammation of joints due to uric acid crystals.
Statement II is false. Gout is caused by the accumulation of uric acid crystals, not calcium salts.
Loss of bone mass is a feature of osteoporosis.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: During contraction of a skeletal muscle fibre, the I band gets reduced while the A band retains its length.
Statement II: During contraction, the Z lines attached to the actin filaments are pulled inwards towards the centre of the A band.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Thin filaments slide inward, so the I band shortens. The A band equals the length of the thick filaments, so it stays the same.
Statement II is correct. Cross bridges pull the actin filaments towards the centre of the A band, and the Z lines attached to them are pulled inward. This shortens the sarcomere.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder that primarily affects which of the following?
questions.explanation:
NCERT describes myasthenia gravis as an autoimmune disorder affecting the neuromuscular junction (motor-end plate).
This leads to fatigue, weakening and paralysis of skeletal muscle.
It does not damage joints or bone matrix. Those are affected in arthritis, gout and osteoporosis.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements about the human axial skeleton is INCORRECT?
options: The vertebral column is dorsally placed, and each vertebra has a neural canal through which the spinal cord passes
Floating ribs are attached dorsally to the thoracic vertebrae and join the seventh rib ventrally through hyaline cartilage
The sternum is a flat bone located on the ventral midline of the thorax
The thoracic vertebrae, ribs and sternum together form the rib cage
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct. The vertebral column is dorsal, and the spinal cord runs through the neural canal of each vertebra.
(2) Incorrect. Joining the 7th rib through hyaline cartilage describes ribs 8–10, the vertebrochondral ribs. Floating ribs (11th and 12th) have no ventral connection at all.
(3) Correct. The sternum is a flat bone on the ventral midline of the thorax.
(4) Correct. These three components together form the rib cage.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The human axial skeleton has 80 bones. If the hyoid and all the ear ossicles of both ears are excluded, how many bones of the axial skeleton remain?
questions.explanation:
Breakdown of the 80 bones: skull 22, hyoid 1, ear ossicles 3 × 2 = 6, vertebrae 26, sternum 1, ribs 12 × 2 = 24.
Check: 22 + 1 + 6 + 26 + 1 + 24 = 80.
Bones excluded: 1 hyoid + 6 ossicles = 7.
Remaining: 80 − 7 = 73.
Option 76 is the error you get by counting the ossicles of only one ear.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Flagellar movement is involved in all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Maintenance of water current in the canal system of sponges
Removal of inhaled dust particles from the trachea
questions.explanation:
NCERT gives three examples of flagellar movement: swimming of spermatozoa, maintenance of water current in the canal system of sponges, and locomotion of the protist Euglena.
Dust is removed from the trachea by the coordinated beating of cilia of the ciliated epithelium. This is ciliary movement, not flagellar movement.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to NCERT, repeated activation of a skeletal muscle can lead to fatigue. What is the immediate cause of this fatigue?
options: Accumulation of lactic acid formed by anaerobic breakdown of glycogen
Accumulation of carbon dioxide formed by aerobic breakdown of glucose
Depletion of myoglobin from the sarcoplasm
Loss of calcium ions from the sarcoplasmic reticulum into the blood
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that repeated activation of muscles leads to accumulation of lactic acid in them. This lactic acid comes from the anaerobic breakdown of glycogen, and it causes fatigue.
Option (2) is tempting, but carbon dioxide from aerobic respiration is not the cause given.
Options (3) and (4) are not mentioned as causes of fatigue.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a myosin monomer (meromyosin), the heavy meromyosin (HMM) refers to:
options: The entire monomer except the head
The globular head together with the short arm
The region that binds the M line
questions.explanation:
Each meromyosin has two parts: a globular head with a short arm, and a tail.
The head with its short arm is called heavy meromyosin (HMM).
The tail is called light meromyosin (LMM), so option (1) describes LMM.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A person shows rapid spasms, or wild contractions, of muscles. According to NCERT, which condition is this, and what causes it?
options: Myasthenia gravis; autoimmune attack on the neuromuscular junction
Muscular dystrophy; low $Ca^{++}$ in body fluid
questions.explanation:
Tetany is defined as rapid spasms (wild contractions) in muscle.
NCERT gives its cause as a low level of $Ca^{++}$ in body fluid, not a high level.
Myasthenia gravis causes fatigue and weakening of muscle, not spasms.
Muscular dystrophy is a progressive degeneration of muscle, mostly genetic in origin.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Each fore limb and each hind limb of a human contains 30 bones. However, the fore limb has 8 carpals while the hind limb has only 7 tarsals. Which hind-limb bone makes up the count to 30?
questions.explanation:
Fore limb: humerus, radius, ulna, 8 carpals, 5 metacarpals and 14 phalanges = 30.
Hind limb: femur, tibia, fibula, 7 tarsals, 5 metatarsals and 14 phalanges = 29.
The cup-shaped patella (knee cap) adds 1, giving 30.
The fibula has a counterpart in the forearm, so it does not explain the difference.
The coxal bone is part of the girdle, and the acetabulum is a cavity, not a bone.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the thin filament is INCORRECT?
options: It contains two F-actins helically wound around each other
Troponin is a simple protein that forms the main backbone of the thin filament
Two filaments of tropomyosin run close to the F-actins throughout their length
Troponin is distributed at regular intervals on the tropomyosin
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: two F-actins are helically wound to each other.
(2) Incorrect: troponin is a complex protein. It is located at regular intervals on tropomyosin. The backbone of the thin filament is formed by the F-actins.
(3) Correct: two tropomyosin filaments run along the full length of the F-actins.
(4) Correct: this matches the NCERT description of troponin.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Actin filaments of a myofibril are commonly called 'thin filaments' because:
options: they are located only in the H zone of the sarcomere
they are thinner than the myosin filaments
each consists of a single G-actin monomer
they lack any associated regulatory proteins
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that actin filaments are thinner than myosin filaments. Actin filaments are therefore called thin filaments, and myosin filaments are called thick filaments.
The H zone is the part of the thick filaments that is not overlapped by thin filaments, so option (1) is wrong.
Each thin filament contains two F-actins, which are polymers of G-actin. It also carries tropomyosin and troponin, so options (3) and (4) are wrong.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (joint location) with List-II (type of joint):
List-I
(a) Between the flat bones of the cranium
(b) Between adjacent vertebrae
(c) Between the carpals
(d) Between the carpal and metacarpal of the thumb
List-II
(i) Gliding joint
(ii) Cartilaginous joint
(iii) Saddle joint
(iv) Fibrous joint
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
(a) Cranial bones are fused end-to-end by sutures of dense fibrous connective tissue. This is a fibrous joint, which allows no movement: (iv).
(b) Adjacent vertebrae are joined by cartilage. This cartilaginous joint allows limited movement: (ii).
(c) The joints between the carpals are gliding joints: (i).
(d) The joint between the carpal and metacarpal of the thumb is a saddle joint: (iii).
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which neurotransmitter is released at the motor-end plate and generates an action potential in the sarcolemma of a skeletal muscle fibre?
questions.explanation:
A neural signal reaching the neuromuscular junction (motor-end plate) releases acetylcholine.
Acetylcholine generates an action potential in the sarcolemma. This action potential spreads through the muscle fibre.
The other options are not the transmitter named by NCERT for the motor-end plate.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are features of white muscle fibres as described in NCERT?
(i) Pale or whitish appearance
(ii) Very little myoglobin
(iii) Few mitochondria
(iv) High amount of sarcoplasmic reticulum
(v) Dependence on anaerobic process for energy
(vi) Large oxygen store used for ATP production
questions.explanation:
(i) Yes: white fibres look pale or whitish.
(ii) Yes: they have very little myoglobin.
(iii) Yes: they have few mitochondria.
(iv) Yes: they have a large amount of sarcoplasmic reticulum.
(v) Yes: they depend on anaerobic processes for energy.
(vi) No: a large oxygen store used for ATP production is a feature of red fibres.
So 5 of the 6 are features of white fibres.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The cranium, which forms the hard protective outer covering of the human brain, is made up of how many bones?
questions.explanation:
The skull has two sets of bones, cranial and facial, totalling 22.
There are 8 cranial bones, and they form the cranium that protects the brain.
The facial region has 14 skeletal elements, so 14 is the facial count, not the cranial count.
22 is the total for the whole skull.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Coordinated movement of cilia in the trachea helps remove dust particles and foreign substances inhaled with air.
Statement II: The passage of ova through the female reproductive tract is brought about by flagellar movement.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The trachea is lined by ciliated epithelium, and its cilia beat in a coordinated way to sweep out dust and inhaled foreign particles.
Statement II is incorrect. NCERT states that ciliary movement, not flagellar movement, helps the ova pass through the female reproductive tract.
Flagellar movement is used, for example, by swimming spermatozoa.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to the sliding filament theory, how does a skeletal muscle fibre contract?
options: By shortening of the thick myosin filaments
By sliding of the thin filaments over the thick filaments
By coiling and folding of the actin filaments
By sliding of the thick filaments past the Z lines
questions.explanation:
The sliding filament theory states that a muscle fibre contracts when the thin (actin) filaments slide over the thick (myosin) filaments.
The filaments themselves do not shorten or fold. Their overlap increases.
Thick filaments stay in the A band and do not move past the Z lines. Option (1) is the common misconception.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The human axial skeleton has 80 bones. Consider only the skull region: all skull bones together with the hyoid and the ear ossicles of both ears. How many bones does this region contribute?
questions.explanation:
The skull has 8 cranial + 14 facial bones, which gives 22.
The hyoid adds 1 bone, bringing the total to 23.
Each middle ear has 3 ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes), so the two ears add 6 bones. The total becomes 29.
Check against 80: 29 + 26 vertebrae + 1 sternum + 24 ribs = 80.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Skeletal muscles are called striated muscles because they show a striped appearance under the microscope.
Statement II: Visceral muscles help to transport gametes through the genital tract.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: the striped appearance of skeletal muscle under the microscope is the reason for the name 'striated'.
Statement II is correct: visceral muscles assist the movement of food through the digestive tract and of gametes through the genital tract.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Skeletal muscle fibres appear striated under the microscope.
Reason (R): Myofibrils show alternate light I bands containing actin and dark A bands containing myosin.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: skeletal muscles have a striped appearance, which is why they are called striated muscles.
R is true: each myofibril has alternate light (I, actin) and dark (A, myosin) bands.
NCERT states that the striated appearance is due to the distribution pattern of actin and myosin. So R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (region of the human vertebral column) with List-II (number of vertebrae):
List-I: (A) Cervical (B) Thoracic (C) Lumbar (D) Sacral
List-II: (i) 5 (ii) 12 (iii) 1 (fused) (iv) 7
questions.explanation:
Cervical vertebrae number 7, so A matches (iv).
Thoracic vertebrae number 12, so B matches (ii).
Lumbar vertebrae number 5, so C matches (i).
The sacrum is a single fused bone, so D matches (iii).
Together with the 1 fused coccyx, these make 26 vertebrae.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about contractile proteins of skeletal muscle are correct?
(i) Each thin filament consists of two F-actins helically wound around each other.
(ii) Two filaments of tropomyosin run close to the F-actins throughout their length.
(iii) Troponin forms a continuous sheath covering the entire length of the actin filament.
(iv) The cross arm projecting from the thick filament is formed by the light meromyosin.
(v) The myosin head carries binding sites for ATP as well as active sites for actin.
(vi) In a resting muscle, tropomyosin itself masks the myosin-binding sites on actin.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: a thin filament has two helically wound F-actins.
(ii) Correct: two tropomyosin filaments run along its whole length.
(iii) Incorrect: troponin is a complex protein placed at regular intervals on tropomyosin. It is not a continuous sheath.
(iv) Incorrect: the cross arm is the HMM (head and short arm), not the LMM.
(v) Correct: the head is an ATPase with ATP-binding sites and active sites for actin.
(vi) Incorrect: a subunit of troponin, not tropomyosin, does the masking.
So 3 statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): During contraction of a skeletal muscle fibre, the Z lines of a sarcomere move closer to each other.
Reason (R): The thin filaments attached to the Z lines are pulled towards the centre of the A band by the cross bridges.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The sarcomere (Z to Z) shortens during contraction, so the Z lines come closer.
R is true. Cross bridges pull the actin filaments towards the centre of the A band.
The thin filaments are firmly attached to the Z lines, so this pull drags the Z lines inwards. R therefore correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.question: How many carpals (wrist bones) are present in each human fore limb?

According to NCERT, each fore limb has 8 carpals (wrist bones), 5 metacarpals (palm bones) and 14 phalanges (digits).
The number 7 belongs to the tarsals (ankle bones) of the hind limb.

questions.question: Which one of the following is a characteristic feature of white muscle fibres?
options: Dependence mainly on aerobic ATP production
questions.explanation:
White fibres have very little myoglobin, so they look pale or whitish.
They have few mitochondria but a large amount of sarcoplasmic reticulum.
They depend on anaerobic processes for energy.
Options (1), (2) and (4) are all features of red fibres, not white fibres.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A very thin transverse section is cut through a myofibril exactly at the level of the H zone (away from the M line) of a resting sarcomere. Which filaments would be seen in this section?
options: No filaments, only the elastic fibre of the Z line
questions.explanation:
At rest, the thin filaments overlap only the free ends of the thick filaments.
The H zone is defined as the central part of the thick filaments that is not overlapped by thin filaments.
A cut through the H zone therefore shows only thick (myosin) filaments.
Both filament types would be seen only in the overlap regions of the A band. Only thin filaments would be seen in the I band.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Muscles with characteristic striations and involuntary are
options: Muscles in the wall of alimentary canal
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists three muscle types.
Skeletal muscles are striated and voluntary. The muscles assisting locomotion and the eyelid muscles belong here, so options (3) and (4) are out.
Visceral muscles, such as those in the alimentary canal wall, are smooth and involuntary, so option (1) is out.
Cardiac muscle, found in the heart, is the only type that is both striated and involuntary.
Answer: (2)

questions.question: Each 'F' actin of a thin filament is a polymer of which of the following monomeric units?

NCERT: each thin filament has two 'F' (filamentous) actins wound helically around each other.
Each 'F' actin is a polymer of monomeric 'G' (globular) actins.
Meromyosins are the monomers of the thick (myosin) filament, not of actin, so (1) is wrong.
Tropomyosin and troponin are accessory proteins that lie on the thin filament. They are not its monomers.

questions.question: Which of the following is the NCERT example of a hinge joint?

NCERT gives the knee joint as its example of a hinge joint.
The shoulder joint is a ball and socket joint.
The joint between the atlas and the axis is a pivot joint.
The joints between the carpals are gliding joints.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Myasthenia gravis
(b) Tetany
(c) Osteoporosis
(d) Gout
List-II
(i) Uric acid crystals in joints
(ii) Low $Ca^{++}$ in body fluid
(iii) Autoimmune disorder of neuromuscular junction
(iv) Decreased bone mass
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
(a) Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction, so it matches (iii).
(b) Tetany is caused by low $Ca^{++}$ in body fluid, so it matches (ii).
(c) Osteoporosis is marked by decreased bone mass, so it matches (iv).
(d) Gout is caused by uric acid crystals in joints, so it matches (i).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following movements in the human body is brought about by ciliary movement rather than by muscular movement?
options: Movement of the jaws during chewing
Passage of ova through the female reproductive tract
Movement of the tongue during speech
Movement of the limbs during walking
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists three types of movement shown by human cells: amoeboid, ciliary and muscular.
Ciliary movement occurs in tubular organs lined by ciliated epithelium. It helps the passage of ova through the female reproductive tract and clears dust from the trachea.
Movement of the jaws, tongue and limbs needs the contraction of muscles, so these are muscular movements.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During the initiation of skeletal muscle contraction, the calcium ions released into the sarcoplasm bind to:
options: A subunit of troponin on the actin filament
questions.explanation:
A rise in Ca++ in the sarcoplasm leads to calcium binding with a subunit of troponin on the actin filaments.
This binding removes the masking of the active sites for myosin on actin.
Tropomyosin runs alongside F-actin, but Ca++ does not bind to it directly. The myosin head binds actin and ATP, not Ca++.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The thick filament of a myofibril is a polymer of which monomeric proteins?
questions.explanation:
NCERT: each myosin (thick) filament is a polymerised protein.
It is made of many monomeric proteins called meromyosins.
G-actins polymerise to form F-actin, which belongs to the thin filament, not the thick one.
Tropomyosin and troponin are also associated with the thin filament.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the organisation of a myofibril is incorrect?
options: Thin filaments are firmly attached to the Z line
The Z line is located in the centre of the A band
A and I bands are arranged alternately throughout the length of the myofibril
Actin and myosin filaments run parallel to each other and to the longitudinal axis of the myofibril
questions.explanation:
Option (1) is correct: NCERT states that thin filaments are firmly attached to the Z line.
Option (2) is incorrect: the Z line bisects the I band. The structure at the middle of the A band is the M line.
Option (3) is correct: A and I bands alternate along the whole myofibril.
Option (4) is correct: both proteins are rod-like and parallel to each other and to the long axis.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following is not a disorder of bone?
questions.explanation:
Arthritis is inflammation of the joints, the junctions between bones.
Osteoporosis is an age-related loss of bone mass, often linked to low oestrogen. It makes bones brittle and more likely to fracture.
Rickets is softening of bones in children due to vitamin D deficiency.
Atherosclerosis is the deposition of fat, cholesterol and calcium in the walls of arteries. It narrows the lumen, so it is a disorder of blood vessels, not bone.
Answer: (4)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 20 (MCQ Q10)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statement is incorrect?
options: Heart muscles are striated and involuntary
The muscles of hands and legs are striated and voluntary
The muscles located in the inner walls of alimentary canal are striated and involuntary
Muscles located in the reproductive tracts are unstriated and involuntary
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: cardiac muscle is striated and involuntary.
(2) Correct: limb muscles are skeletal muscles, which are striated and voluntary.
(3) Incorrect: the inner walls of the alimentary canal contain visceral (smooth) muscle. This muscle is unstriated (non-striated) and involuntary, not striated.
(4) Correct: reproductive tract muscles are visceral, so they are unstriated and involuntary.
Answer: (3)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 20 (MCQ Q11)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the globular head of a meromyosin?
options: It stores calcium ions needed for contraction
It forms part of the light meromyosin
It is firmly attached to the 'Z' line
It is an active ATPase enzyme with binding sites for ATP and active sites for actin
questions.explanation:
NCERT: the globular head is an active ATPase enzyme. It has binding sites for ATP and active sites for actin.
Calcium ions are stored in the sarcoplasmic reticulum, not in the myosin head.
The head belongs to heavy meromyosin, not light meromyosin.
It is the thin filaments, not the myosin heads, that attach to the Z line.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The H zone of a sarcomere becomes narrower during muscle contraction.
Reason (R): The thick myosin filaments shorten during muscle contraction.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The H zone is the central part of the thick filaments not overlapped by thin filaments. As the thin filaments slide inward, the overlap increases and the H zone narrows.
R is false. Myosin filaments do not shorten. That is why the A band keeps its length.
The narrowing of the H zone is caused by sliding, not by filament shortening.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Myasthenia gravis
(B) Muscular dystrophy
(C) Tetany
(D) Gout
List-II
(I) Accumulation of uric acid crystals in joints
(II) Low $Ca^{++}$ in body fluid
(III) Autoimmune disorder affecting neuromuscular junction
(IV) Progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle, mostly genetic
questions.explanation:
A–III: myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune attack on the neuromuscular junction. It causes fatigue and paralysis.
B–IV: muscular dystrophy is progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle, mostly genetic.
C–II: tetany is rapid spasms caused by low $Ca^{++}$ in body fluid.
D–I: gout is joint inflammation caused by deposition of uric acid crystals.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder.
(ii) Muscular dystrophy is mostly due to a genetic disorder.
(iii) Tetany results from a high level of $Ca^{++}$ in body fluid.
(iv) Osteoporosis is characterised by increased bone mass.
(v) Gout is due to accumulation of uric acid crystals in joints.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: myasthenia gravis is autoimmune.
(ii) Correct: muscular dystrophy is mostly genetic.
(iii) Incorrect: tetany is due to low $Ca^{++}$, not high.
(iv) Incorrect: osteoporosis involves decreased bone mass.
(v) Correct: gout is caused by uric acid crystals in joints.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which vertebra articulates with the occipital condyles of the human skull?
questions.explanation:
The first vertebra of the vertebral column is the atlas.
The atlas articulates with the two occipital condyles of the skull.
The axis is the second vertebra. It forms a pivot joint with the atlas, not with the skull.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about muscles is incorrect?
options: Muscles have been classified on the basis of location, appearance and nature of regulation of their activities
Many cardiac muscle cells assemble in a branching pattern to form cardiac muscle
On the basis of location, muscles are classified as striated and non-striated
Skeletal muscles are primarily involved in locomotory actions and changes of body posture
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: NCERT names location, appearance and regulation as the criteria for classifying muscles.
(2) Correct: cardiac muscle cells assemble in a branching pattern.
(3) Incorrect: striated versus non-striated is a classification by appearance. By location, muscles are skeletal, visceral and cardiac.
(4) Correct: skeletal muscles mainly serve locomotion and changes of posture.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to NCERT, a common cause of osteoporosis is:
options: Accumulation of uric acid in bones
questions.explanation:
Osteoporosis is an age-related disorder with decreased bone mass and a greater chance of fractures.
NCERT names decreased levels of estrogen as a common cause.
A rise in estrogen is the opposite of the stated cause.
Uric acid accumulation is the cause of gout, a joint disorder.
Answer: (3)
