questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In the cross-bridge cycle, binding of a new ATP molecule to the myosin head causes the cross bridge to break.
Statement II: Muscle relaxation occurs when Ca++ ions are pumped back into the sarcoplasmic cisternae, which results in masking of the actin filaments.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. After the power stroke, myosin releases ADP and Pi. A new ATP then binds and the cross bridge is broken.
Statement II is correct. The cycle continues until Ca++ is pumped back into the sarcoplasmic cisternae. Actin is then masked again and the Z lines return to their original position.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about skeletal muscle are correct?
(i) Muscle is a specialised tissue of ectodermal origin.
(ii) Muscles contribute about 40-50 per cent of the body weight of a human adult.
(iii) Fascia is a collagenous connective tissue layer.
(iv) Myofibrils lie parallel to one another in the sarcoplasm.
(v) Each fascicle consists of only one muscle fibre.
questions.explanation:
(i) Incorrect: muscle is of mesodermal origin, not ectodermal.
(ii) Correct: muscles form about 40-50% of adult body weight.
(iii) Correct: fascia is collagenous connective tissue.
(iv) Correct: myofibrils are arranged in parallel in the sarcoplasm.
(v) Incorrect: each fascicle contains a number of muscle fibres.
So three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following bones belong to the axial skeleton?
Sternum, Clavicle, Atlas, Scapula, A rib, Patella, Occipital bone, Ilium
questions.explanation:
The axial skeleton is made of the skull, vertebral column, sternum and ribs.
Axial bones in the list:
- Sternum
- Atlas (a vertebra)
- A rib
- Occipital bone (cranium)
Appendicular bones in the list: clavicle and scapula (pectoral girdle), patella (lower limb) and ilium (pelvic girdle).
Total axial bones = 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Each 'F' (filamentous) actin of a thin filament is formed by the polymerisation of:
questions.explanation:
NCERT: each F-actin is a polymer of monomeric G (globular) actins.
Two such F-actins are helically wound to form the backbone of the thin filament.
Meromyosins are the monomers of the thick (myosin) filament, not of actin.
Tropomyosin and troponin are accessory proteins that lie along the F-actin; they are not its building blocks.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following events of skeletal muscle contraction in the correct sequence:
(i) Ca++ binds to troponin and the active sites on actin are unmasked
(ii) Acetylcholine is released at the motor-end plate
(iii) Myosin head binds actin to form a cross bridge
(iv) Action potential spreads through the sarcolemma and Ca++ is released into the sarcoplasm
(v) Actin filaments are pulled towards the centre of the A band
questions.explanation:
Step 1: The neural signal releases acetylcholine at the motor-end plate (ii).
Step 2: An action potential spreads through the fibre and Ca++ is released (iv).
Step 3: Ca++ binds troponin, unmasking the active sites on actin (i).
Step 4: The myosin head binds the exposed sites, forming cross bridges (iii).
Step 5: The cross bridges pull actin towards the centre of the A band (v).
Option (4) fails because cross bridges cannot form before the sites are unmasked.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The joints between the flat bones of the cranium do not allow any movement.
Reason (R): These flat bones fuse end-to-end through dense fibrous connective tissue in the form of sutures.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Cranial bones are joined by fibrous joints, and fibrous joints permit no movement.
R is true. The flat skull bones are fused end-to-end by dense fibrous connective tissue, forming sutures.
R correctly explains A: this rigid fibrous fusion is exactly what prevents movement.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: How many tarsals (ankle bones) are present in one human lower limb?
questions.explanation:
Each lower limb has femur, tibia, fibula, tarsals, metatarsals, phalanges and the patella.
The ankle bones are the tarsals, and each limb has 7 of them.
The tempting option 8 is the number of carpals (wrist bones) in the upper limb.
5 is the number of metatarsals, and 14 is the number of phalanges.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A hypothetical toxin prevents Ca++ ions from binding to the troponin subunit, but it does not affect nerve impulses, acetylcholine release, Ca++ release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, or the ATPase activity of myosin. What would most likely happen when the muscle fibre is stimulated?
options: The fibre would remain permanently contracted because cross bridges could not break
F-actin would depolymerise into G-actin, so the thin filaments would disappear
Myosin-binding sites on actin would stay masked, so cross bridges would not form and the fibre would not contract
Myosin heads would bind actin normally but would be unable to hydrolyse ATP
questions.explanation:
Normally, Ca++ binds a troponin subunit and removes the masking of the myosin-binding sites on actin.
If Ca++ cannot bind troponin, these sites remain masked even though Ca++ has been released.
Myosin heads therefore cannot attach to actin, no cross bridges form, and no sliding or contraction occurs.
The ATPase activity of myosin is stated to be unaffected, so option (4) is wrong.
Nothing affects actin polymerisation, so option (2) is wrong.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A skeletal muscle fibre is regarded as a syncytium.
Reason (R): Each skeletal muscle fibre has a single nucleus enclosed within the sarcolemma.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: a muscle fibre is a syncytium.
R is false: the sarcoplasm of a muscle fibre contains many nuclei, not one.
In fact, being multinucleate is the very reason the fibre is called a syncytium.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (location) with List-II (type of joint):
List-I
(a) Between the flat skull bones
(b) Between adjacent vertebrae
(c) Between the carpals
(d) Between the atlas and the axis
List-II
(i) Pivot joint
(ii) Fibrous joint
(iii) Gliding joint
(iv) Cartilaginous joint
questions.explanation:
(a) The flat skull bones are joined by sutures, which are fibrous joints: (ii).
(b) Adjacent vertebrae are joined by cartilage, forming cartilaginous joints: (iv).
(c) The joints between the carpals are gliding joints: (iii).
(d) The joint between the atlas and the axis is a pivot joint: (i).
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which structural type of joint has a fluid-filled cavity between the articulating surfaces of the two bones?
questions.explanation:
NCERT defines synovial joints by a fluid-filled synovial cavity between the articulating surfaces of two bones.
This cavity allows considerable movement.
Fibrous joints and sutures join bones with dense fibrous connective tissue and have no cavity.
Cartilaginous joints join bones with cartilage and have no fluid-filled cavity.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which bone of the human body is described in NCERT as the longest bone?
questions.explanation:
The femur (thigh bone) is the longest bone of the body.
It articulates with the acetabulum of the pelvic girdle.
The tibia and fibula are lower leg bones, and the humerus is the upper arm bone. All three are shorter than the femur.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: A human being has a total of six ear ossicles.
Statement II: The 22 bones of the human skull are made up of 8 cranial bones, 13 facial bones and the hyoid bone.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: each middle ear has 3 ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes), so there are 6 in total.
Statement II is incorrect: the 22 skull bones are 8 cranial and 14 facial elements.
The hyoid is counted separately from these 22.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Cardiac muscles are involuntary in nature.
Reason (R): Cardiac muscles do not show striations under the microscope.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The nervous system does not directly control cardiac muscle activity, so cardiac muscle is involuntary.
R is false. Cardiac muscles are striated in appearance.
Note also that whether a muscle is voluntary depends on nervous control, not on whether it has striations.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) G-actin
(b) Light meromyosin
(c) Cross arm
(d) Troponin
List-II
(i) Complex protein present at regular intervals on tropomyosin
(ii) Tail portion of a myosin monomer
(iii) Monomer that polymerises to form F-actin
(iv) HMM projecting outwards from the surface of the thick filament
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation:
(a) G-actin is the globular monomer that polymerises to form F-actin, so (a)-(iii).
(b) Light meromyosin is the tail of the meromyosin, so (b)-(ii).
(c) The cross arm is the HMM (head and short arm) projecting outwards from the thick filament surface, so (c)-(iv).
(d) Troponin is a complex protein spaced at regular intervals on tropomyosin, so (d)-(i).
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Cardiac muscles are described as involuntary muscles.
Reason (R): The nervous system does not control the activities of cardiac muscles directly.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT classifies cardiac muscles as involuntary.
R is true: NCERT states that the nervous system does not directly control the activities of cardiac muscles.
R is the reason they are called involuntary, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A sarcomere is examined first at rest and then during contraction. Which set of observations is consistent with the sliding filament theory?
options: A band shortens, I band remains unchanged, H zone shortens
A band remains unchanged, I band shortens, H zone shortens, Z lines come closer
A band remains unchanged, I band shortens, H zone remains unchanged
Both thick and thin filaments shorten, so A band, I band and H zone all shorten
questions.explanation:
In contraction, thin filaments slide over thick filaments towards the centre of the A band. The filaments themselves do not shorten.
The A band equals the length of the thick filaments, so it stays the same.
The I band (thin filaments only) shrinks as overlap increases.
The H zone (central thick filament not overlapped) also narrows.
The Z lines attached to actin are pulled inwards, so the sarcomere shortens.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A toxin blocks the pumping of Ca++ ions back into the sarcoplasmic cisternae, but leaves the rest of the contraction machinery unaffected. What is the most likely effect on a skeletal muscle fibre after it has been stimulated?
options: The fibre cannot contract because acetylcholine is not released
The fibre stays contracted, because the active sites on actin remain unmasked and cross bridge cycling continues
The A band shortens while the I band lengthens
The fibre relaxes immediately because troponin masks actin without Ca++
questions.explanation:
Relaxation occurs only when Ca++ is pumped back into the sarcoplasmic cisternae. This re-masks the active sites on actin, and the Z lines return to their original position.
If the pump is blocked, Ca++ stays bound to troponin and the sites stay exposed.
Cross bridge formation and breakage keep repeating, so the fibre fails to relax.
Acetylcholine release is unaffected, and the A band never shortens.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Macrophages and leucocytes exhibit
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists three types of movement in human cells: amoeboid, ciliary and muscular.
Macrophages and leucocytes move by forming pseudopodia through streaming of protoplasm, as in Amoeba. Cytoskeletal elements such as microfilaments are involved. This is amoeboid movement.
Ciliary movement is seen in the trachea and the fallopian tubes. Flagellar movement is used by sperm to swim.
Answer: (3)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 20 (MCQ Q9)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (type of movement) with List-II (example):
List-I
(a) Amoeboid
(b) Ciliary
(c) Flagellar
(d) Muscular
List-II
(i) Water current in the canal system of sponges
(ii) Movement of jaws and tongue
(iii) Leucocytes in blood
(iv) Removal of foreign substances from the trachea
questions.explanation:
(a) Amoeboid matches (iii): leucocytes move by pseudopodia.
(b) Ciliary matches (iv): tracheal cilia remove dust and foreign substances.
(c) Flagellar matches (i): flagella maintain the water current in sponge canals.
(d) Muscular matches (ii): movements of the jaws and tongue need muscles.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The joint between adjacent vertebrae is a cartilaginous joint and permits only limited movement.
Statement II: The joint between the carpal and the metacarpal of the thumb is a gliding joint.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: adjacent vertebrae are joined by cartilage, which allows limited movement.
Statement II is incorrect: the carpal–metacarpal joint of the thumb is a saddle joint.
Gliding joints occur between the carpals themselves.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(a) G-actin
(b) Troponin
(c) Heavy meromyosin (HMM)
(d) Light meromyosin (LMM)
List-II
(i) Tail of the myosin monomer
(ii) Globular head with a short arm
(iii) Monomer that polymerises to form F-actin
(iv) Masks myosin-binding sites on actin in resting state
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
(a) G-actin: the monomeric globular actins polymerise into F-actin, so (iii).
(b) Troponin: at rest, one of its subunits masks the active sites for myosin on actin, so (iv).
(c) HMM: this is the globular head with its short arm, so (ii).
(d) LMM: this is the tail of the meromyosin, so (i).
Option (2) reverses HMM and LMM, which is the common confusion.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements correctly describe a single sarcomere in the resting state?
(i) It contains one complete A band flanked by two half I bands.
(ii) The M line lies within the H zone, at its centre.
(iii) The I band consists of thin (actin) filaments.
(iv) Thick filaments are anchored to the Z lines at both ends.
(v) The H zone forms a part of the A band.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: a sarcomere spans Z line to Z line. This gives a central A band with half an I band on each side.
(ii) Correct: the M line is at the middle of the A band, which is also the centre of the H zone.
(iii) Correct: the I band is the actin-containing light band.
(iv) Incorrect: thin filaments attach to the Z line, while thick filaments are held together at the M line.
(v) Correct: the H zone is the central part of the thick filaments, so it lies within the A band.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The 8th, 9th and 10th pairs of ribs do not join the sternum directly but join the seventh rib through hyaline cartilage.
Statement II: Ribs are called bicephalic because they articulate dorsally with the vertebral column and ventrally with the sternum.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. These three pairs are the vertebrochondral (false) ribs, and they join the seventh rib through hyaline cartilage.
Statement II is incorrect. A rib is called bicephalic because its dorsal end has two articulation surfaces. Its connections to the vertebral column and sternum are not the reason.
Also, floating ribs have no ventral connection at all.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following events of skeletal muscle contraction in the correct sequence:
(i) A new ATP binds to the myosin head and the cross bridge breaks
(ii) Calcium binds to a subunit of troponin, unmasking active sites on actin
(iii) Acetylcholine is released at the motor-end plate
(iv) Myosin head binds to actin, forming a cross bridge, and pulls actin towards the centre of the A band
(v) An action potential spreads through the fibre and $Ca^{++}$ is released into the sarcoplasm
questions.explanation:
Step 1: The neural signal releases acetylcholine at the motor-end plate (iii).
Step 2: An action potential spreads along the sarcolemma, and $Ca^{++}$ is released into the sarcoplasm (v).
Step 3: $Ca^{++}$ binds troponin, exposing the myosin-binding sites on actin (ii).
Step 4: The myosin head, energised by ATP hydrolysis, forms a cross bridge and pulls actin inward (iv).
Step 5: A new ATP binds and the cross bridge breaks (i).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: When the calcium level rises in the sarcoplasm of a stimulated muscle fibre, Ca++ binds to which component, thereby removing the masking of active sites for myosin?
questions.explanation:
In resting muscle, a subunit of troponin masks the myosin-binding active sites on actin.
When Ca++ rises, it binds to this troponin subunit.
This binding unmasks the active sites.
Tropomyosin carries troponin but is not the Ca++-binding site.
The myosin head binds actin, not Ca++.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The 8th, 9th and 10th pairs of ribs do not articulate directly with the sternum. Instead, they join the seventh rib through hyaline cartilage. These ribs are called:
questions.explanation:
The first 7 pairs are true ribs. They are joined to the sternum by hyaline cartilage.
Pairs 8–10 reach the sternum only indirectly, by joining the 7th rib through hyaline cartilage. These are the vertebrochondral (false) ribs.
Pairs 11–12 have no ventral connection, so they are called floating ribs.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Acetylcholine
(b) Calcium ions
(c) Binding of a new ATP to the myosin head
(d) Hydrolysis of ATP by the myosin head
List-II
(i) Breaking of the cross bridge
(ii) Provides energy for the myosin head to bind actin
(iii) Generates action potential in the sarcolemma
(iv) Unmasking of active sites on actin
questions.explanation:
(a) Acetylcholine generates an action potential in the sarcolemma, so (a)-(iii).
(b) Ca++ binds troponin and unmasks the active sites on actin, so (b)-(iv).
(c) After ADP and Pi are released, a new ATP binds the myosin head and the cross bridge breaks, so (c)-(i).
(d) Energy from ATP hydrolysis lets the myosin head bind actin and form a cross bridge, so (d)-(ii).
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the sarcomere are correct?
(i) A sarcomere is the portion of a myofibril between two successive M lines.
(ii) The M line is a thin fibrous membrane that holds the thick filaments together in the middle of the A band.
(iii) Each sarcomere has one central A band flanked by two half I bands.
(iv) In the resting state, the thin filaments partially overlap the free ends of the thick filaments.
(v) Myosin filaments are thinner than actin filaments.
questions.explanation:
(i) Incorrect: a sarcomere lies between two successive Z lines.
(ii) Correct: the M line holds the thick filaments together at the middle of the A band.
(iii) Correct: a sarcomere has a central A band with half an I band on each side, ending at the Z lines.
(iv) Correct: at rest, thin filaments overlap the ends of the thick filaments, leaving the H zone free.
(v) Incorrect: actin filaments are the thinner ones.
So three statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A student examines a diagram of a resting sarcomere and traces it from one Z line to the next Z line along its length. Which sequence correctly lists the regions encountered?
options: Z line → half A band → I band with M line at its centre → half A band → Z line
Z line → H zone → A band → H zone → Z line
Z line → I band → M line → I band → Z line
Z line → half I band → region of overlap in A band → H zone with M line at its centre → region of overlap in A band → half I band → Z line
questions.explanation:
The Z line bisects the I band, so each Z line has half an I band next to it.
The A band lies centrally. Its outer parts are where thin filaments overlap the thick filaments.
The central H zone contains only thick filaments, and the M line runs through its middle.
Option (1) swaps the positions of the A and I bands. Option (3) omits the A band entirely.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A student lists all the bones of one human lower limb but leaves out the phalanges and the knee cap. How many bones remain in the list?
questions.explanation:
One lower limb has 30 bones: femur (1), tibia (1), fibula (1), tarsals (7), metatarsals (5), phalanges (14) and patella (1).
Removing the 14 phalanges and the 1 patella leaves 30 − 15.
The remaining bones are 1 + 1 + 1 + 7 + 5 = 15.
The option 16 would wrongly keep the patella in the count.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I:
A. Myasthenia gravis
B. Tetany
C. Gout
D. Osteoporosis
List-II:
(i) Accumulation of uric acid crystals in joints
(ii) Decreased estrogen levels as a common cause
(iii) Autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction
(iv) Low $Ca^{++}$ in body fluid
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
A. Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction, so A-(iii).
B. Tetany is rapid muscle spasm caused by low $Ca^{++}$ in body fluid, so B-(iv).
C. Gout is joint inflammation caused by uric acid crystals, so C-(i).
D. Osteoporosis is age-related loss of bone mass, commonly linked to decreased estrogen, so D-(ii).
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a patient, antibodies of the body's own immune system attack the motor-end plate. This leads to fatigue, weakening and eventually paralysis of skeletal muscles. Which step of muscle contraction is most directly impaired?
options: Hydrolysis of ATP by the globular head of myosin
Generation of an action potential in the sarcolemma by acetylcholine released at the junction
Pumping of $Ca^{++}$ back into the sarcoplasmic cisternae
Polymerisation of G-actin to form F-actin
questions.explanation:
The description fits myasthenia gravis, an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction (motor-end plate).
At this junction, a neural signal releases acetylcholine. Acetylcholine generates an action potential in the sarcolemma, which starts contraction.
If this transmission fails, the action potential does not arise. As a result, $Ca^{++}$ is not released and no cross bridges form, so the muscle weakens.
The other options are events inside the fibre, not at the junction.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
A. Z line
B. M line
C. H zone
D. I band
List-II
(i) Light, isotropic band containing actin
(ii) Central part of thick filaments not overlapped by thin filaments
(iii) Thin fibrous membrane holding thick filaments together in the middle of the A band
(iv) Elastic fibre bisecting the I band
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation:
A-(iv): The Z line is an elastic fibre in the centre of the I band, and it bisects that band.
B-(iii): The M line is a thin fibrous membrane that holds the thick filaments together in the middle of the A band.
C-(ii): The H zone is the central part of the thick filaments that thin filaments do not overlap.
D-(i): The I band is the light, isotropic band made of actin.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match the following and mark the correct option.
Column I: A. Fast muscle fibres; B. Slow muscle fibres; C. Actin filament; D. Sarcomere
Column II: i. Myoglobin; ii. Lactic acid; iii. Contractile unit; iv. I-band
questions.explanation:
A. Fast (white) fibres have little myoglobin and rely on anaerobic respiration, so lactic acid builds up: A–ii.
B. Slow (red) fibres are rich in the oxygen-storing pigment myoglobin: B–i.
C. Thin actin filaments form the light I-band: C–iv.
D. The sarcomere, between two Z-lines, is the functional contractile unit of a myofibril: D–iii.
Option (2) wrongly pairs actin with the contractile unit and the sarcomere with the I-band.
Answer: (3)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 20 (MCQ Q1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Cardiac muscle fibres appear striated under the microscope.
Statement II: Cardiac muscles are voluntary because the nervous system directly controls their activity.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Cardiac muscles are striated in appearance, and their cells assemble in a branching pattern.
Statement II is incorrect. Cardiac muscles are involuntary because the nervous system does not control their activity directly.
So cardiac muscle is striated like skeletal muscle but involuntary like visceral muscle.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Muscle is a specialised tissue. From which embryonic germ layer does it originate?
questions.explanation:
NCERT describes muscle as a specialised tissue of mesodermal origin.
Ectoderm gives rise to tissues such as the nervous system and epidermis, so it is not the source of muscle.
Endoderm forms linings such as those of the gut, so it does not fit either.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the human appendicular skeleton is incorrect?
options: The scapula is a large triangular flat bone situated in the dorsal part of the thorax between the second and seventh ribs
The clavicle is a long slender bone with two curvatures
The patella is a cup-shaped bone that covers the knee dorsally
The femur is the longest bone of the body
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: NCERT places the scapula dorsally, between the 2nd and 7th ribs.
(2) Correct: the clavicle (collar bone) is long and slender with two curvatures.
(3) Incorrect: the patella (knee cap) covers the knee ventrally, not dorsally.
(4) Correct: the femur, or thigh bone, is the longest bone.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about contractile proteins are correct?
(i) Each 'F' actin is a polymer of monomeric 'G' actins.
(ii) A thin filament has two 'F' actins helically wound around each other.
(iii) Troponin is distributed at regular intervals on tropomyosin.
(iv) Light meromyosin (LMM) consists of the globular head and short arm.
(v) The globular head of myosin has binding sites for ATP and active sites for actin.
(vi) In the resting state, tropomyosin masks the active binding sites for myosin on actin.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: each 'F' actin is a polymer of 'G' actins.
(ii) Correct: two 'F' actins are helically wound to form the thin filament.
(iii) Correct: troponin occurs at regular intervals on tropomyosin.
(iv) Incorrect: the head and short arm form heavy meromyosin (HMM); LMM is the tail.
(v) Correct: the head is an ATPase with ATP binding sites and actin-binding sites.
(vi) Incorrect: at rest, a subunit of troponin masks these sites, not tropomyosin.
So 4 statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Bone has a very hard matrix, whereas cartilage has a slightly pliable matrix. According to NCERT, the pliability of the cartilage matrix is due to:
questions.explanation:
Bone and cartilage are both specialised connective tissues.
Bone is very hard because its matrix contains calcium salts.
Cartilage is slightly pliable because its matrix contains chondroitin salts.
Calcium salts is the tempting wrong option, but those salts make bone hard, not cartilage pliable.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding red and white muscle fibres is INCORRECT?
options: Red fibres contain plenty of mitochondria.
White fibres appear pale because they have very little myoglobin.
White fibres have more mitochondria than red fibres, which compensates for their low myoglobin.
Red and white fibres are distinguished primarily on the basis of myoglobin content.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: red fibres have plenty of mitochondria.
(2) Correct: white fibres have very little myoglobin, so they look pale.
(3) Incorrect: white fibres have FEW mitochondria. What they have in large amount is sarcoplasmic reticulum, and they rely on anaerobic energy.
(4) Correct: NCERT classifies red and white fibres primarily by their myoglobin content.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are synovial joints?
Knee joint; joint between the atlas and the axis; sutures of the cranium; joint between adjacent vertebrae; joints between the carpals; joint between the carpal and metacarpal of the thumb
questions.explanation:
Synovial joints: the knee (hinge), atlas–axis (pivot), between the carpals (gliding) and carpal–metacarpal of the thumb (saddle). That makes 4.
Not synovial: cranial sutures are fibrous joints.
Not synovial: the joint between adjacent vertebrae is cartilaginous.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I:
A. True ribs
B. Vertebrochondral ribs
C. Floating ribs
D. Bicephalic nature of ribs
List-II:
(i) Two articulation surfaces on the dorsal end
(ii) Not connected ventrally
(iii) Join the seventh rib through hyaline cartilage
(iv) Connected ventrally to the sternum through hyaline cartilage
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
A. True ribs are pairs 1 to 7. They attach ventrally to the sternum by hyaline cartilage, so A-(iv).
B. Vertebrochondral (false) ribs are pairs 8 to 10. They join the seventh rib by hyaline cartilage, so B-(iii).
C. Floating ribs are pairs 11 and 12. They have no ventral connection, so C-(ii).
D. Each rib has two articulation surfaces on its dorsal end, which is why it is called bicephalic, so D-(i).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A hypothetical toxin completely blocks the pumping of $Ca^{++}$ ions back into the sarcoplasmic cisternae of a skeletal muscle fibre after it has been stimulated. Which outcome is most likely, provided ATP keeps being supplied?
options: Troponin keeps masking the myosin-binding sites on actin, so the muscle cannot contract at all
The active sites on actin stay exposed and cross-bridge cycling continues, so the muscle fails to relax
Acetylcholine release at the motor-end plate stops, so no action potential is generated
The A bands shorten while the I bands keep their length
questions.explanation:
Normally, $Ca^{++}$ binds a subunit of troponin and unmasks the myosin-binding sites on actin. Relaxation happens only when $Ca^{++}$ is pumped back into the sarcoplasmic cisternae and the sites are masked again.
If $Ca^{++}$ stays in the sarcoplasm, the sites remain exposed. With ATP available, cross bridges keep forming and breaking, so the muscle stays contracted and does not relax.
Option 1 describes the opposite situation, a lack of $Ca^{++}$.
Option 4 is wrong because A bands always keep their length during contraction.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The plasma membrane that lines each skeletal muscle fibre is known as:
questions.explanation:
Each muscle fibre is lined by a plasma membrane called the sarcolemma.
The sarcolemma encloses the sarcoplasm, which is the cytoplasm of the fibre.
A sarcomere is the contractile unit between two Z lines.
Fascia is a connective tissue layer around fascicles, not a cell membrane.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A toxin blocks the release of calcium ions from the sarcoplasmic reticulum of skeletal muscle fibres. Acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction is not affected. What is the most likely result when the motor neuron is stimulated?
options: No action potential is generated in the sarcolemma
An action potential spreads in the sarcolemma, but troponin keeps the myosin-binding sites on actin masked, so the muscle does not contract
Cross bridges form normally, but they cannot break, so the muscle stays contracted
The A band shortens while the I band stays the same
questions.explanation:
Acetylcholine still generates an action potential in the sarcolemma, so option (1) is wrong.
Normally the action potential causes Ca++ to be released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
This Ca++ binds a subunit of troponin and unmasks the active sites on actin.
Without Ca++ release, the sites stay masked, myosin heads cannot form cross bridges, and no contraction occurs.
The A band never changes length during contraction in any case.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The bones forming the human cranium do not move against each other.
Reason (R): The flat skull bones are fused end-to-end by dense fibrous connective tissue in the form of sutures.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: the cranial bones are joined by fibrous joints, which allow no movement.
R is true: the flat skull bones fuse end-to-end through sutures made of dense fibrous connective tissue.
This fusion by fibrous tissue is exactly why movement is not possible, so R explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of white muscle fibres?
options: Dependence mainly on aerobic respiration for ATP
questions.explanation:
White fibres contain very little myoglobin, so they look pale.
They have few mitochondria and depend on anaerobic processes for energy.
According to NCERT, they do have a high amount of sarcoplasmic reticulum.
Options (1), (2) and (4) describe red (aerobic) fibres instead.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In a resting sarcomere, the H zone contains thick filaments but no thin filaments.
Reason (R): At rest, the edges of the thin filaments overlap only the free ends of the thick filaments, leaving the central part of the thick filaments uncovered.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The H zone is defined as the central part of the thick filaments that is not overlapped by thin filaments.
R is true. In the resting state, the thin filaments on either side partially overlap only the free ends of the thick filaments.
The uncovered middle region left by this overlap is exactly the H zone, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements about the contractile proteins of skeletal muscle is correct?
options: Each thin filament consists of two G-actin chains helically wound around each other
The heavy meromyosin, made of the globular head and short arm, projects from the thick filament as the cross arm
In the resting state, tropomyosin itself masks the myosin-binding active sites on actin
The light meromyosin (tail) bears the ATP binding sites and acts as an ATPase
questions.explanation:
(1) Incorrect: a thin filament has two F-actins wound helically; each F-actin is a polymer of G-actin monomers.
(2) Correct: the HMM (globular head with short arm) projects outward at regular distances and angles as the cross arm.
(3) Incorrect: in the resting state it is a subunit of troponin that masks the active sites.
(4) Incorrect: the ATPase activity and ATP binding sites are on the globular head (HMM), not on the LMM tail.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
A cross-sectional diagram of a skeletal muscle shows the following:
- Several bundles (Y) bound together by a common layer (X).
- Each bundle contains many cells (Z), with blood capillaries among them.
- Each cell Z is bounded by a membrane (W).
Which statement about this diagram is INCORRECT?
options: Y represents fascicles, and X is collagenous connective tissue
W is a layer of collagenous connective tissue called fascia
Z contains many parallel myofibrils in its sarcoplasm
questions.explanation:
X is the fascia, a collagenous layer, and Y are the fascicles, so (1) is correct.
Z are muscle fibres, which are multinucleate syncytia, so (2) is correct.
Z contains many parallel myofibrils in the sarcoplasm, so (4) is correct.
W is the sarcolemma, the plasma membrane of the fibre, not collagenous fascia, so (3) is incorrect.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In a resting skeletal muscle fibre, myosin heads do not form cross bridges with actin.
Reason (R): In the resting state, a subunit of troponin masks the active binding sites for myosin on the actin filaments.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: cross bridges form only after contraction has been triggered.
R is true: at rest, a troponin subunit covers the myosin-binding sites on actin.
R explains A. Because these sites are masked, myosin heads cannot attach to actin.
Only when Ca++ binds troponin is the masking removed, which allows cross bridges to form.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following human cells shows amoeboid movement?
options: Ciliated epithelial cells of the trachea
questions.explanation:
NCERT names macrophages and leucocytes in blood as the specialised human cells that show amoeboid movement.
This movement is brought about by pseudopodia, as in Amoeba.
Spermatozoa are the tempting option, but they swim by flagellar movement, not by pseudopodia.
Tracheal epithelial cells show ciliary movement, and erythrocytes are not given as an example.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The passage of ova through the human female reproductive tract is facilitated by which type of movement?
questions.explanation:
Many internal tubular organs, including the female reproductive tract, are lined by ciliated epithelium.
NCERT states that ciliary movement facilitates the passage of ova through the female reproductive tract.
The ovum does not move itself, so it neither forms pseudopodia nor bears a flagellum.
Flagellar movement is used by spermatozoa, not ova.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a myofibril of skeletal muscle, which structure is the functional unit of contraction?
options: Sarcomere, the portion of the myofibril between two successive Z lines
Muscle fibre, the portion enclosed by the sarcolemma
Fascicle, a bundle of muscle fibres held by fascia
The portion of the myofibril between two successive M lines
questions.explanation:
NCERT defines the sarcomere as the portion of a myofibril between two successive Z lines. It is the functional unit of contraction.
The muscle fibre is the anatomical unit, not the functional unit. A fascicle is a bundle of fibres.
The tempting option (4) is wrong because the M line lies in the middle of the A band. A sarcomere is bounded by Z lines, not M lines.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Muscular dystrophy involves progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle.
Reason (R): Muscular dystrophy is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT defines muscular dystrophy as progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle.
R is false. NCERT says muscular dystrophy is mostly due to a genetic disorder.
The autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction is myasthenia gravis.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (type of synovial joint) with List-II (location):
List-I
(a) Ball and socket joint
(b) Pivot joint
(c) Gliding joint
(d) Saddle joint
List-II
(i) Between carpals
(ii) Between carpal and metacarpal of thumb
(iii) Between humerus and pectoral girdle
(iv) Between atlas and axis
questions.explanation:
(a) The head of the humerus fits into the glenoid cavity of the pectoral girdle, forming a ball and socket joint, so (a)-(iii).
(b) The atlas rotates on the axis at a pivot joint, so (b)-(iv).
(c) The carpals glide over one another, so (c)-(i).
(d) The carpal-metacarpal joint of the thumb is a saddle joint, so (d)-(ii).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly arranges the levels of skeletal muscle organisation from the largest to the smallest?
options: Muscle → Muscle fibre → Fascicle → Myofibril → Sarcomere
Muscle → Fascicle → Muscle fibre → Myofibril → Sarcomere
Muscle → Fascicle → Myofibril → Muscle fibre → Sarcomere
Fascicle → Muscle → Muscle fibre → Sarcomere → Myofibril
questions.explanation:
A whole muscle is made of many fascicles, which are held together by fascia.
Each fascicle contains many muscle fibres (muscle cells).
Each fibre contains many parallel myofibrils in its sarcoplasm.
Each myofibril is a series of sarcomeres, the functional units of contraction.
So the correct order is muscle → fascicle → fibre → myofibril → sarcomere.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Muscle tissue can be stretched and can then return to its original shape. Which pair of muscle properties listed by NCERT describes these two abilities, in that order?
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists four properties of muscle: excitability, contractility, extensibility and elasticity.
Extensibility is the ability to be stretched.
Elasticity is the ability to recoil to the original shape after stretching.
Excitability (responding to a stimulus) and contractility (shortening) describe different abilities.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The acetabulum receives the head of the thigh bone.
Reason (R): The acetabulum is a depression present on the scapula below the acromion.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The acetabulum is the cavity to which the femur (thigh bone) articulates.
R is false. The acetabulum lies on the coxal bone, at the point where the ilium, ischium and pubis fuse.
The depression on the scapula below the acromion is the glenoid cavity, which receives the humerus.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A drug that selectively disrupts microfilaments, but not microtubules, is applied to a preparation of different human cells. Which activity is most directly affected?
options: Beating of cilia in tracheal epithelium
Ciliary transport of ova in the female reproductive tract
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that amoeboid movement by pseudopodia, as seen in macrophages and leucocytes, involves microfilaments.
Cilia and flagella are outgrowths of the cell membrane whose core is made of microtubules (Chapter 8).
So tracheal ciliary beating, ciliary transport of ova and sperm flagellar swimming would not be directly hit.
Only pseudopodial movement depends directly on microfilaments.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Six disorders are grouped by the structure mainly affected, as described in NCERT: myasthenia gravis, muscular dystrophy, tetany, arthritis, osteoporosis and gout. Which grouping is correct?
options: Skeletal muscle: myasthenia gravis, muscular dystrophy, tetany; Joints: arthritis, gout; Bone mass: osteoporosis
Skeletal muscle: myasthenia gravis, tetany; Joints: arthritis, gout, muscular dystrophy; Bone mass: osteoporosis
Skeletal muscle: muscular dystrophy, tetany; Joints: arthritis; Bone mass: osteoporosis, gout
Skeletal muscle: myasthenia gravis, muscular dystrophy; Joints: arthritis, tetany; Bone mass: osteoporosis, gout
questions.explanation:
Myasthenia gravis causes weakness and paralysis of skeletal muscle. Muscular dystrophy degenerates skeletal muscle. Tetany produces spasms in muscle. All three are muscle disorders.
Arthritis and gout are both inflammations of joints.
Osteoporosis is the only one defined by decreased bone mass.
The other options misplace muscular dystrophy, tetany or gout.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(a) Locomotory structures are always different from the structures used for other types of movement.
(b) Hydra uses its tentacles both for capturing prey and for locomotion.
(c) Beating of cilia in the human trachea is a form of locomotion.
(d) Locomotion requires a perfectly coordinated activity of the muscular, skeletal and neural systems.
Which of the above are correct?
questions.explanation:
(a) Incorrect: NCERT says locomotory structures need not differ from those used for other movements. Examples are Paramoecium cilia, Hydra tentacles and human limbs.
(b) Correct: Hydra tentacles serve both prey capture and locomotion.
(c) Incorrect: tracheal cilia move dust, but the body does not change place, so this is not locomotion.
(d) Correct: NCERT states this directly.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the human vertebral column is incorrect?
options: It is formed by 26 serially arranged vertebrae and is dorsally placed
The sacral and coccygeal regions are each represented by a single fused unit
The thoracic region has 5 vertebrae and the lumbar region has 12 vertebrae
Each vertebra has a central neural canal through which the spinal cord passes
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: there are 26 vertebrae and the column is dorsal.
(2) Correct: the sacrum is 1 fused unit and the coccyx is 1 fused unit.
(3) Incorrect: the numbers are swapped. The thoracic region has 12 vertebrae and the lumbar region has 5.
(4) Correct: the spinal cord passes through the neural canal.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are listed in NCERT as general purposes of locomotion in animals?
(i) Search of food
(ii) Search of a mate
(iii) Escape from enemies or predators
(iv) Finding suitable breeding grounds
(v) Digestion of ingested food
(vi) Seeking favourable climatic conditions
questions.explanation:
NCERT says locomotion is generally for food, shelter, mate, suitable breeding grounds, favourable climatic conditions, or escape from enemies or predators.
(i), (ii), (iii), (iv) and (vi) are therefore correct.
(v) is wrong. Digestion is a function of the digestive system, not a purpose of changing location.
The count is 5.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following pairs is incorrect?
options: Hinge joint: between Humerus and Pectoral girdle
Pivot joint : between atlas and axis
Saddle joint : between carpals and metacarpals of thumb
questions.explanation:
(1) Incorrect: the humerus and the pectoral girdle (glenoid cavity) form a ball and socket joint, not a hinge joint.
(2) Correct: the atlas–axis joint is a pivot joint.
(3) Correct: the joints between carpals are gliding joints.
(4) Correct: the carpal–metacarpal joint of the thumb is a saddle joint.
So pair (1) is the incorrect one.
Answer: (1)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 20 (MCQ Q7)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the sarcomere of a resting skeletal muscle is incorrect?
options: The A band is the dark, anisotropic band containing myosin
The Z line is an elastic fibre located in the centre of the I band
Thin filaments are firmly attached to the Z line
The H zone contains both thick and thin filaments overlapping each other
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: the A band is dark and anisotropic, and it contains myosin.
(2) Correct: the Z line bisects the I band.
(3) Correct: actin (thin) filaments are firmly attached to the Z line.
(4) Incorrect: the H zone is the central part of the thick filaments that is NOT overlapped by thin filaments. It contains only thick filaments.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The 8th, 9th and 10th pairs of ribs are joined directly to the sternum by hyaline cartilage.
Statement II: Each rib is called bicephalic because its dorsal end has two articulation surfaces.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. Ribs 8–10 do not articulate directly with the sternum. They join the 7th rib through hyaline cartilage, which is why they are called vertebrochondral (false) ribs.
Statement II is correct. Each rib has two articulation surfaces at its dorsal end, so it is bicephalic.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about red and white muscle fibres is incorrect?
options: Red fibres have a high content of myoglobin.
Red fibres contain plenty of mitochondria.
White fibres have a large amount of sarcoplasmic reticulum.
White fibres depend mainly on aerobic processes for energy.
questions.explanation:
Option (1) is correct: red fibres have a high myoglobin content, which gives them their reddish colour.
Option (2) is correct: red fibres have plenty of mitochondria, which use the stored oxygen to make ATP. This is why they are called aerobic muscles.
Option (3) is correct: white fibres have little myoglobin and few mitochondria but a lot of sarcoplasmic reticulum.
Option (4) is incorrect: white fibres depend on anaerobic processes for energy, not aerobic ones.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Amoeboid movement is effected by pseudopodia formed by the streaming of protoplasm.
Statement II: Cytoskeletal elements such as microfilaments play no role in amoeboid movement.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. In macrophages and leucocytes, as in Amoeba, pseudopodia form by protoplasmic streaming.
Statement II is incorrect. NCERT specifically states that cytoskeletal elements like microfilaments are involved in amoeboid movement.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following events of skeletal muscle contraction in the correct sequence:
(a) $Ca^{++}$ binds to a subunit of troponin, unmasking active sites on actin
(b) Acetylcholine is released at the motor-end plate
(c) An action potential spreads through the sarcolemma
(d) $Ca^{++}$ is released into the sarcoplasm
(e) Myosin head binds actin forming a cross bridge, pulling actin towards the centre of the A band
(f) A new ATP binds to myosin and the cross bridge breaks
options: b → c → d → a → e → f
b → d → c → a → e → f
c → b → d → a → f → e
b → c → a → d → e → f
questions.explanation:
A neural signal releases acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction (b).
This generates an action potential in the sarcolemma (c), which causes release of $Ca^{++}$ from the sarcoplasmic reticulum (d).
$Ca^{++}$ binds troponin and exposes the myosin-binding sites on actin (a).
The energised myosin head binds actin, forms a cross bridge and pulls actin inwards (e).
After ADP and Pi are released, a new ATP binds and the cross bridge breaks (f).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following belong to the axial skeleton?
Hyoid, Malleus, Clavicle, Sternum, Scapula, Sacrum, Patella, Ribs
questions.explanation:
The axial skeleton includes the skull with the hyoid and ear ossicles, the vertebral column, the sternum and the ribs.
Axial: hyoid, malleus, sternum, sacrum (a vertebral unit) and ribs. That makes 5.
Appendicular: the clavicle and scapula belong to the pectoral girdle, and the patella belongs to the hind limb.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the human skeleton are correct?
(i) Each limb is made of 30 bones.
(ii) The cranium is formed by 8 bones.
(iii) Both carpals and tarsals are 8 in number in each limb.
(iv) Each limb has 14 phalanges.
(v) The facial region of the skull has 14 skeletal elements.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: each fore limb and each hind limb has 30 bones.
(ii) Correct: there are 8 cranial bones.
(iii) Incorrect: there are 8 carpals but only 7 tarsals.
(iv) Correct: each limb has 14 phalanges.
(v) Correct: there are 14 facial elements, and 8 + 14 = 22 skull bones.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Ribs are attached to
questions.explanation:
There are 12 pairs of ribs. Each rib is attached dorsally to a thoracic vertebra.
Ventrally, the first 7 pairs (true ribs) join the sternum through hyaline cartilage. The 8th–10th pairs join it indirectly through the cartilage of the 7th rib.
The scapula and clavicle belong to the pectoral girdle, and the ilium is part of the pelvic girdle. None of these bears ribs.
So the sternum is the correct choice.
Answer: (2)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 20 (MCQ Q2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Approximately what fraction of the body weight of a human adult is contributed by muscles?
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that muscles contribute about 40-50 per cent of the body weight of a human adult.
This is close to half the body mass, so the lower ranges are too small.
The 60-70 per cent range overestimates the share.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The head of the humerus fits into the glenoid cavity of the scapula. What type of joint does this form?
questions.explanation:
The glenoid cavity lies below the acromion of the scapula.
It articulates with the head of the humerus to form the shoulder joint.
NCERT gives the joint between the humerus and the pectoral girdle as its example of a ball and socket joint.
A hinge joint is exemplified by the knee, not the shoulder.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Muscle fibres that are rich in myoglobin and mitochondria can also be called:
questions.explanation:
Red fibres have a high myoglobin content and plenty of mitochondria.
These mitochondria use the large amount of stored oxygen to produce ATP, so NCERT also calls these fibres aerobic muscles.
Option (1) describes white fibres instead.
Options (3) and (4) refer to how muscles are classified by control and appearance, not to red fibres.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following events of skeletal muscle contraction in the correct order:
(a) Release of Ca++ into the sarcoplasm
(b) Release of acetylcholine at the motor-end plate
(c) Action potential spreads through the muscle fibre
(d) Myosin head binds actin to form a cross bridge
(e) Ca++ binds troponin and unmasks the active sites on actin
questions.explanation:
First, the neural signal releases acetylcholine at the motor-end plate (b).
This generates an action potential that spreads through the fibre (c).
The action potential causes Ca++ release into the sarcoplasm (a).
Ca++ binds troponin and unmasks the active sites (e).
The myosin head then binds actin, forming a cross bridge (d).
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Acetabulum
(b) Glenoid cavity
(c) Acromion
(d) Pubic symphysis
List-II
(i) Articulates with the clavicle
(ii) Contains fibrous cartilage
(iii) Receives the thigh bone
(iv) Receives the head of the humerus
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation:
(a) Acetabulum is the cavity of the coxal bone where the femur articulates, so (iii).
(b) The glenoid cavity of the scapula receives the head of the humerus, so (iv).
(c) The acromion, the expanded end of the scapular spine, articulates with the clavicle, so (i).
(d) The pubic symphysis, where the two pelvic halves meet ventrally, contains fibrous cartilage, so (ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Macrophages and leucocytes in blood show amoeboid movement brought about by pseudopodia.
Statement II: Cytoskeletal elements such as microfilaments take part in amoeboid movement.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT names macrophages and leucocytes as specialised body cells that move by pseudopodia formed through streaming of protoplasm, as in Amoeba.
Statement II is correct. NCERT states that microfilaments are also involved in amoeboid movement.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A skeletal muscle fibre is described as a syncytium because:
options: It is enclosed by collagenous fascia
It contains alternate dark and light bands
It stores calcium ions in its endoplasmic reticulum
questions.explanation:
A syncytium is a single cell-like unit that contains many nuclei in a common cytoplasm.
The sarcoplasm of a muscle fibre has many nuclei, so the fibre is a syncytium.
The banding pattern explains striation, not the syncytial nature.
The calcium store and the fascia are separate features of muscle organisation.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During a movement brought about by muscles, what role does the joint play?
options: It conducts the nerve impulse to the muscle
questions.explanation:
Muscles generate the force for a movement.
The movement is carried out through joints, and the joint acts as the fulcrum.
Force generation is a property of muscles, not joints, so option (1) is wrong.
Calcium is stored in the sarcoplasmic reticulum, and nerve impulses reach the muscle through motor neurons.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
During contraction of a skeletal muscle fibre, how many of the following changes occur in a sarcomere?
(i) Length of the I band decreases
(ii) Length of the A band stays the same
(iii) The H zone becomes narrower
(iv) The Z lines move closer to each other
(v) The thick filaments themselves shorten
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: thin filaments slide inward, so the I band shortens.
(ii) Correct: the A band equals the length of the thick filaments, which does not change.
(iii) Correct: the thin filaments slide over the central region, so the H zone narrows.
(iv) Correct: the Z lines are pulled inward and the sarcomere shortens.
(v) Incorrect: filaments only slide past each other; neither type shortens.
Number of changes that occur = 4.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A motor unit is best defined as:
options: A motor neuron together with all the muscle fibres connected to it
The junction between a motor neuron and the sarcolemma
The portion of a myofibril between two successive Z lines
A muscle bundle held together by fascia
questions.explanation:
NCERT defines a motor unit as a motor neuron along with the muscle fibres connected to it.
Option (2) describes the neuromuscular junction (motor-end plate).
Option (3) describes a sarcomere.
Option (4) describes a fascicle.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Each human rib is described as bicephalic.
Reason (R): Each rib has two articulation surfaces on its dorsal end.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT calls each rib bicephalic.
R is true: each rib has two articulation surfaces at its dorsal end, where it connects to the vertebral column.
The word 'bicephalic' means 'two-headed', so the name comes directly from these two dorsal articulating surfaces.
Therefore R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The dark band seen on a myofibril under the microscope is known as the:
options: H zone, which contains actin only
A band (anisotropic band), which contains myosin
questions.explanation:
Myofibrils show alternate dark and light bands, produced by the distribution of actin and myosin.
The dark band is the A (anisotropic) band and contains myosin.
The light band is the I (isotropic) band and contains actin, so option (1) describes the light band, not the dark one.
The Z line is an elastic fibre, not a band of tropomyosin.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Motor-end plate
(b) Sarcoplasmic reticulum
(c) Globular head of myosin
(d) Troponin (resting state)
List-II
(i) Masks active binding sites for myosin on actin
(ii) Active ATPase enzyme with actin-binding sites
(iii) Junction of motor neuron and sarcolemma
(iv) Store house of calcium ions
questions.explanation:
(a)-(iii): The motor-end plate is the junction between a motor neuron and the sarcolemma.
(b)-(iv): The sarcoplasmic reticulum stores Ca++.
(c)-(ii): The myosin head is an active ATPase and has active sites for actin.
(d)-(i): At rest, a subunit of troponin masks the myosin-binding sites on actin.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: ATPase of the muscle is located in
questions.explanation:
Each myosin molecule (meromyosin) has a globular head with a short arm, called heavy meromyosin.
This head is an active ATPase enzyme. It also has binding sites for ATP and for actin, and it forms cross-bridges during contraction.
Actin is the thin filament and has only the binding sites for myosin. Troponin is a regulatory protein that binds $Ca^{2+}$ and has no ATPase activity.
Answer: (3)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 20 (MCQ Q4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The globular head of a meromyosin is an active ATPase enzyme.
Statement II: Each thin filament of a myofibril is formed by the polymerisation of many meromyosin monomers.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The myosin head is an active ATPase. It has binding sites for ATP and active sites for actin.
Statement II is incorrect. Meromyosins polymerise to form the thick (myosin) filament.
The thin filament is made of two F-actins, which are polymers of G-actin, along with tropomyosin and troponin.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The reddish appearance of some skeletal muscles is due to a high content of which oxygen-storing pigment?
questions.explanation:
Muscle contains a red-coloured, oxygen-storing pigment called myoglobin. Muscles rich in myoglobin look reddish and are called red fibres.
Haemoglobin is also a red oxygen-carrying pigment, but it is found in RBCs, not in the muscle fibre itself.
Cytochrome and melanin do not give muscle its red colour.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Synovial joints permit considerable movement and help in locomotion.
Statement II: The joint between adjacent vertebrae in the vertebral column is a synovial joint.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: the fluid-filled synovial cavity allows considerable movement, so these joints help in locomotion.
Statement II is incorrect: adjacent vertebrae are joined by cartilage.
This makes the intervertebral joint a cartilaginous joint, which permits only limited movement.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is true?
options: Head of humerus bone articulates with acetabulum of pectoral girdle.
Head of humerus bone articulates with the glenoid cavity of pectoral girdle.
Head of humerus bone articulates with acetabulum of pelvic girdle.
Head of humerus bone articulates with a glenoid cavity of pelvic girdle.
questions.explanation:
The pectoral girdle is made of the clavicle and the scapula.
The scapula has a depression called the glenoid cavity. The head of the humerus fits into it to form the ball-and-socket shoulder joint.
The acetabulum is a cavity in the pelvic girdle, formed by the fused ilium, ischium and pubis. It receives the head of the femur, not the humerus.
So options (1), (3) and (4) mismatch the bone or the girdle.
Answer: (2)
