questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A muscle fibre is stimulated and cross bridges form normally. Its supply of ATP is then completely exhausted while Ca++ is still present in the sarcoplasm. Based on the cross-bridge cycle, what is the most likely immediate state of the fibre?
options: Actin sites become masked again and the fibre relaxes at once
Myosin heads detach from actin, but the fibre cannot contract again
Myosin heads remain attached to actin, so the fibre stays contracted and cannot relax
Thin filaments slide back, so the A band becomes shorter
questions.explanation:
A new ATP must bind to the myosin head to break the cross bridge.
Without ATP, myosin heads already bound to actin cannot detach. The cross bridges persist and the sarcomere stays shortened.
Option (1) fails because masking of actin requires Ca++ to be pumped back into the sarcoplasmic cisternae.
Option (2) fails because detachment itself needs ATP. Option (4) fails because the A band length never changes.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In humans, the 11th and 12th pairs of ribs are not connected ventrally to anything. These ribs are called:
questions.explanation:
Ribs 1–7 are true ribs. They are joined ventrally to the sternum through hyaline cartilage.
Ribs 8–10 are vertebrochondral (false) ribs. They join the 7th rib ventrally.
Ribs 11–12 have no ventral connection, so they are called floating ribs.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): White muscle fibres depend mainly on anaerobic processes for energy.
Reason (R): White muscle fibres contain only a small amount of sarcoplasmic reticulum.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. White fibres have very little myoglobin and few mitochondria, so they rely on anaerobic processes for energy.
R is false. NCERT states that white fibres have a high amount of sarcoplasmic reticulum.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The human skull is described as dicondylic.
Reason (R): The skull articulates with the superior region of the vertebral column through two occipital condyles.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT describes the human skull as dicondylic.
R is true. The skull joins the atlas, the first vertebra, by means of two occipital condyles.
The term 'dicondylic' means 'having two condyles', so R directly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) I band
(b) A band
(c) Z line
(d) H zone
List-II
(i) Central part of thick filaments not overlapped by thin filaments
(ii) Isotropic light band containing actin
(iii) Anisotropic dark band containing myosin
(iv) Elastic fibre to which thin filaments are firmly attached
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation:
(a) I band: the isotropic light band made of actin → (ii).
(b) A band: the anisotropic dark band made of myosin → (iii).
(c) Z line: the elastic fibre bisecting the I band, to which thin filaments are firmly attached → (iv).
(d) H zone: the central region of the thick filaments not overlapped by thin filaments → (i).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are bones of the human hind limb?
Femur, Fibula, Radius, Patella, Tarsals, Ulna, Metatarsals
questions.explanation:
Hind limb bones in the list: femur, fibula, patella, tarsals and metatarsals. That makes 5.
The radius and ulna are bones of the fore limb (forearm).
The patella (knee cap) is counted with the leg bones.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The matrix of cartilage is slightly pliable, unlike the very hard matrix of bone. According to NCERT, this pliability is due to the presence of:
questions.explanation:
Bone and cartilage are both specialised connective tissues.
Bone has a very hard matrix because it contains calcium salts.
Cartilage has a slightly pliable matrix because it contains chondroitin salts.
Calcium salts are the tempting option, but they explain the hardness of bone, not the flexibility of cartilage.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Myoglobin
(b) Lactic acid
(c) High sarcoplasmic reticulum
(d) Plenty of mitochondria
List-II
(i) Feature of white fibres
(ii) Oxygen-storing red pigment
(iii) Feature of red fibres
(iv) Causes muscle fatigue
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation:
(a) Myoglobin is the red, oxygen-storing pigment of muscle, so a-ii.
(b) Lactic acid accumulates after repeated activation and causes fatigue, so b-iv.
(c) A high amount of sarcoplasmic reticulum is a feature of white fibres, so c-i.
(d) Plenty of mitochondria is a feature of red fibres, so d-iii.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Skeletal muscle
(b) Visceral muscle
(c) Cardiac muscle
(d) Fascia
List-II
(i) Smooth and involuntary
(ii) Collagenous connective tissue holding the fascicles together
(iii) Striated and voluntary
(iv) Striated, branched and involuntary
questions.explanation:
(a) Skeletal muscle is striated and under voluntary control: iii.
(b) Visceral muscle is smooth (non-striated) and involuntary: i.
(c) Cardiac muscle is striated, has a branching pattern and is involuntary: iv.
(d) Fascia is the common collagenous connective tissue layer that holds muscle bundles together: ii.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are parts of the human axial skeleton?
Hyoid, Malleus, Sternum, Clavicle, Scapula, Ribs, Patella
questions.explanation:
Hyoid: axial. It is the U-shaped bone at the base of the buccal cavity.
Malleus: axial. It is an ear ossicle of the skull region.
Sternum and ribs: axial. Both are parts of the rib cage.
Clavicle and scapula: appendicular. They belong to the pectoral girdle.
Patella: appendicular. It is the knee cap of the hind limb.
So 4 of the listed bones are axial.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The light band seen on a myofibril is called the ______ and it contains the protein ______.
questions.explanation:
Myofibrils show alternate light and dark bands.
The light band contains actin and is called the I band, or Isotropic band.
The dark band is the A band, or Anisotropic band, and it contains myosin.
Option (4) has the correct name but pairs it with the wrong protein.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which pair of muscle types falls in the same group when muscles are classified by appearance, but in different groups when they are classified by the nature of regulation of their activity?
options: Visceral muscles of the gut and visceral muscles of the genital tract
questions.explanation:
By appearance, skeletal and cardiac muscles are both striated, while visceral muscle is smooth.
By regulation, skeletal muscle is voluntary, while cardiac and visceral muscles are involuntary.
So skeletal and cardiac muscles match in appearance but differ in regulation.
Visceral and cardiac muscles are the reverse case: they differ in appearance but are both involuntary.
Skeletal and visceral muscles differ in both appearance and regulation.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The lactic acid that accumulates in repeatedly activated muscles is produced by aerobic breakdown of glycogen.
Statement II: White muscle fibres, being poor in myoglobin and mitochondria, depend on anaerobic processes for energy.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect: lactic acid comes from the ANAEROBIC breakdown of glycogen. Aerobic breakdown does not produce lactic acid.
Statement II is correct: white fibres have little myoglobin and few mitochondria, so they rely on anaerobic energy production.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: When an action potential spreads through a skeletal muscle fibre, calcium ions enter the sarcoplasm. From which structure are they released?
questions.explanation:
The endoplasmic reticulum of a muscle fibre is called the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
It is the store house of calcium ions.
The action potential triggers release of Ca++ from it into the sarcoplasm.
After contraction, Ca++ is pumped back into the sarcoplasmic cisternae.
Mitochondria supply ATP but are not the Ca++ store named by NCERT.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following bones is NOT a part of the axial skeleton?
questions.explanation:
The axial skeleton (80 bones) consists of the skull, vertebral column, sternum and ribs.
The hyoid bone and the ear ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes) belong to the skull region of the axial skeleton.
The clavicle forms part of the pectoral girdle. Girdles and limb bones make up the appendicular skeleton.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are components of the actin (thin) filament?
G-actin, F-actin, tropomyosin, troponin, heavy meromyosin, light meromyosin
questions.explanation:
Thin filament components:
(i) G-actin: yes, it is the monomer of F-actin.
(ii) F-actin: yes, two are helically wound.
(iii) Tropomyosin: yes, two filaments run along the F-actin.
(iv) Troponin: yes, it lies on tropomyosin.
Heavy and light meromyosin are parts of myosin monomers, so they belong to the thick filament.
The count is 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Red muscle fibres are also called aerobic muscles.
Reason (R): Red fibres contain plenty of mitochondria that can use the large amount of oxygen stored by myoglobin for ATP production.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT states that red fibres can be called aerobic muscles.
R is true: red fibres store a lot of oxygen in myoglobin and have many mitochondria that use this oxygen to make ATP.
It is exactly this oxygen-based (aerobic) ATP production that earns them the name. So R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match the followings and mark the correct option.
Column I: A. Sternum; B. Glenoid Cavity; C. Freely movable joint; D. Cartilaginous joint
Column II: i. Synovial fluid; ii. Vertebrae; iii. Pectoral girdle; iv. Flat bones
questions.explanation:
A. Sternum is a flat bone in the ventral midline of the thorax, so A–iv.
B. The glenoid cavity lies on the scapula, which is part of the pectoral girdle, so B–iii.
C. Freely movable (synovial) joints have a fluid-filled synovial cavity, so C–i.
D. Adjacent vertebrae are joined by cartilage, forming cartilaginous joints, so D–ii.
This gives A-iv, B-iii, C-i, D-ii, which matches option (2).
Answer: (2)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 20 (MCQ Q14)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the total number of bones present in BOTH fore limbs of a human, excluding the phalanges?
questions.explanation:
One fore limb has: humerus (1) + radius (1) + ulna (1) + carpals (8) + metacarpals (5) + phalanges (14) = 30.
Excluding the phalanges: 30 − 14 = 16 bones per limb.
For both fore limbs: 16 × 2 = 32.
The girdles are not counted, because they are separate from the 30 bones of each limb.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Movement and locomotion cannot be studied separately.
Reason (R): In Paramoecium, cilia help in the movement of food through the cytopharynx and also in locomotion.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT concludes that movement and locomotion are linked and cannot be studied separately.
R is true. Paramoecium cilia move food through the cytopharynx and also bring about locomotion.
R explains A. Because the same structure serves both ordinary movement and locomotion, the two processes cannot be separated.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a movement in the human body with the type of movement involved?
options: Engulfing of microbes by macrophages – ciliary movement
Passage of ova through the female reproductive tract – ciliary movement
Movement of leucocytes out of blood vessels – muscular movement
Removal of inhaled dust particles from the trachea – amoeboid movement
questions.explanation:
(1) Incorrect: macrophages show amoeboid movement using pseudopodia.
(2) Correct: ciliated epithelium of the female reproductive tract helps move ova along.
(3) Incorrect: leucocytes move by amoeboid movement, not muscular movement.
(4) Incorrect: dust is cleared from the trachea by the coordinated beating of cilia.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In a myofibril, the Z line is an elastic fibre that bisects the I band.
Statement II: The thick myosin filaments are firmly attached to the Z line.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. An elastic fibre called the Z line lies in the centre of each I band and bisects it.
Statement II is incorrect. The thin (actin) filaments are firmly attached to the Z line. The thick filaments are held together in the middle of the A band by the M line.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following is showing the correct sequential order of vertebrae in the vertebral column of human beings?
questions.explanation:
From the skull downward, the human vertebral column has 26 vertebrae:
7 cervical (neck) → 12 thoracic (chest, bearing ribs) → 5 lumbar (lower back) → 1 sacral (5 fused) → 1 coccygeal (4 fused).
So the order is cervical – thoracic – lumbar – sacral – coccygeal.
The other options misplace the lumbar or sacral region. For example, the sacrum lies below the lumbar vertebrae, not above them.
Answer: (4)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 20 (MCQ Q6)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the type of movable joint present between the atlas and axis?
questions.explanation:
The atlas (1st cervical vertebra) rotates around the odontoid process (dens) of the axis (2nd cervical vertebra).
Rotation of one bone around a peg of another is the defining feature of a pivot joint. This joint lets us turn the head from side to side.
A hinge joint (e.g., elbow) allows only flexion and extension in one plane, not rotation. A saddle joint is found at the thumb, and gliding joints occur between carpals.
Answer: (1)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 20 (MCQ Q3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The glenoid cavity of the scapula articulates with which bone to form the shoulder joint?
questions.explanation:
The glenoid cavity is a depression on the scapula, just below the acromion.
It receives the head of the humerus, forming the shoulder joint, which is a ball and socket joint.
The clavicle articulates with the acromion, not with the glenoid cavity.
The head of the femur fits into the acetabulum of the pelvic girdle.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Visceral (smooth) muscles are typically found in which of the following locations?
options: Attached to the bones of the limbs
Inner walls of the alimentary canal
questions.explanation:
Visceral muscles are located in the inner walls of hollow visceral organs, such as the alimentary canal and the reproductive tract.
Muscles attached to limb bones and the jaw-moving muscles are skeletal muscles.
The wall of the heart contains cardiac muscle, not visceral muscle.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: When a skeletal muscle fibre contracts according to the sliding filament theory, which region of the sarcomere retains its original length?
questions.explanation:
During contraction, thin filaments slide over thick filaments towards the centre of the A band.
The A band corresponds to the full length of the thick filaments, which do not change in length. So the A band retains its length.
The I band and the H zone shrink. The Z–Z distance, which is the sarcomere, also decreases.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about skeletal muscle contraction are correct?
(i) The signal for contraction reaches the muscle from the CNS via a motor neuron.
(ii) The globular head of myosin acts as an ATPase enzyme.
(iii) Cross bridges pull the actin filaments towards the centre of the A band.
(iv) The cross bridge is broken as soon as ADP and Pi are released from the myosin head.
(v) The length of the A band decreases during contraction.
(vi) The sarcoplasmic reticulum stores Ca++ ions.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct. Contraction is initiated by a CNS signal sent via a motor neuron.
(ii) Correct. The myosin head is an active ATPase.
(iii) Correct. Actin filaments are pulled towards the centre of the A band.
(iv) Incorrect. Releasing ADP and Pi only returns myosin to its relaxed state; the cross bridge breaks when a new ATP binds.
(v) Incorrect. The A band retains its length.
(vi) Correct. The sarcoplasmic reticulum is the store house of Ca++.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A motor neuron together with all the muscle fibres connected to it is called a:
questions.explanation:
NCERT defines a motor unit as a motor neuron along with the muscle fibres connected to it.
The motor-end plate, or neuromuscular junction, is only the junction between the motor neuron and the sarcolemma. It is not the neuron plus its fibres.
The sarcomere is the functional unit of contraction inside a myofibril.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between movement and locomotion?
options: All movements are locomotions, but all locomotions are not movements
All locomotions are movements, but all movements are not locomotions
Movement and locomotion are completely unrelated processes
Locomotion is always involuntary, while movement is always voluntary
questions.explanation:
Locomotion is a voluntary movement that changes the place or location of the organism, as in walking, swimming or flying.
Many movements, such as moving the eyelids or jaws, do not change location.
So locomotion is a subset of movement: all locomotions are movements, but not all movements are locomotions.
Option 1 reverses this relationship.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following changes occur in a sarcomere when a skeletal muscle fibre contracts?
(i) The I band becomes shorter
(ii) The H zone becomes shorter
(iii) The A band becomes shorter
(iv) The distance between successive Z lines decreases
(v) The actin filaments themselves become shorter
(vi) The length of the myosin filaments remains unchanged
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: thin filaments slide inwards, so the I band reduces.
(ii) Correct: increased overlap shrinks the H zone, the central non-overlapped part of the thick filaments.
(iii) Incorrect: the A band retains its length.
(iv) Correct: the sarcomere shortens.
(v) Incorrect: filaments slide over each other and do not shorten themselves.
(vi) Correct: myosin filament length stays the same.
Correct changes = 4.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the human body, the joint between the atlas and the axis vertebrae is an example of which type of synovial joint?
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists examples of synovial joints: ball and socket (humerus–pectoral girdle), hinge (knee), pivot (atlas–axis), gliding (between carpals) and saddle (carpal–metacarpal of thumb).
The atlas–axis joint is therefore a pivot joint.
Hinge is tempting because it is also a synovial joint, but NCERT's hinge example is the knee, not the atlas–axis.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: How many bones form the cranium, the hard protective outer covering of the human brain?
questions.explanation:
The skull has 22 bones in total.
These are divided into 8 cranial bones and 14 facial bones.
The 8 cranial bones form the cranium, which protects the brain.
The number 14 refers to the facial elements and 22 is the whole skull, so neither fits.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which neurotransmitter is released at the motor-end plate when a neural signal reaches it, generating an action potential in the sarcolemma?
questions.explanation:
The neuromuscular junction (motor-end plate) is the junction between a motor neuron and the sarcolemma.
When a neural signal arrives there, acetylcholine is released.
Acetylcholine generates an action potential in the sarcolemma.
The other options are not the neurotransmitter NCERT names at the motor-end plate.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A muscle sample looks pale under examination. Its fibres show few mitochondria and an extensive sarcoplasmic reticulum. Based on NCERT, which prediction about this muscle during prolonged, repeated activation is most appropriate?
options: It will rely on oxygen stored in its abundant myoglobin and resist fatigue.
It will rely on anaerobic breakdown of glycogen, so lactic acid will tend to accumulate and cause fatigue.
It will produce most of its ATP in mitochondria, so lactic acid will not form.
It will remain contracted because its extensive sarcoplasmic reticulum cannot pump back Ca$^{2+}$ ions.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Pale colour, few mitochondria and abundant sarcoplasmic reticulum identify this as a white fibre muscle.
Step 2: White fibres depend on anaerobic processes for energy.
Step 3: Anaerobic breakdown of glycogen produces lactic acid. On repeated activation this lactic acid accumulates and causes fatigue.
Option (1) wrongly assumes abundant myoglobin, and option (3) wrongly assumes many mitochondria; both describe red fibres. Option (4) is wrong because the sarcoplasmic reticulum stores Ca$^{2+}$ and does take it back during relaxation.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
A. Hyoid
B. Neural canal
C. Sternum
D. Ear ossicles
List-II
(i) Flat bone on the ventral midline of the thorax
(ii) Malleus, incus and stapes
(iii) U-shaped bone at the base of the buccal cavity
(iv) Passage for the spinal cord
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation:
A-(iii): the hyoid is a single U-shaped bone at the base of the buccal cavity.
B-(iv): the spinal cord passes through the neural canal of each vertebra.
C-(i): the sternum is a flat bone on the ventral midline of the thorax.
D-(ii): the malleus, incus and stapes are the ear ossicles in each middle ear.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Muscle is a specialised tissue that contributes about 40-50 per cent of the body weight of a human adult. From which germ layer does it originate?
questions.explanation:
NCERT describes muscle as a specialised tissue of mesodermal origin.
It makes up about 40-50% of adult human body weight.
Ectoderm mainly forms the epidermis and nervous tissue, so it is wrong.
Endoderm mainly forms the lining of the gut and associated glands, so it is also wrong.
Muscle tissue is not derived from ectoderm or endoderm, which rules out option (4).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Knee joint and elbow joint are examples of
questions.explanation:
Hinge joints allow movement mainly in one plane (flexion and extension), like a door hinge.
Both the knee and the elbow move this way, so they are hinge joints.
A ball and socket joint (shoulder, hip) allows movement in many planes. A pivot joint (atlas–axis) allows rotation, and a saddle joint is found at the thumb.
Answer: (4)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 20 (MCQ Q8)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The glenoid cavity, which receives the head of the humerus to form the shoulder joint, is a part of which bone?
questions.explanation:
The scapula has a ridge called the spine, which projects as a flat process called the acromion.
Below the acromion lies a depression, the glenoid cavity.
The glenoid cavity articulates with the head of the humerus to form the shoulder joint.
The clavicle is the tempting wrong choice. It articulates with the acromion, but it has no glenoid cavity.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The joint between the first and second vertebrae of the vertebral column is a pivot joint.
Reason (R): The first vertebra, the atlas, articulates with the two occipital condyles of the skull.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: the first and second vertebrae are the atlas and the axis, and NCERT names the joint between them as a pivot joint.
R is true: the atlas articulates with the occipital condyles, which is why the human skull is called dicondylic.
However, R describes the skull–atlas articulation, not the atlas–axis joint. So R does not explain A.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a myofibril of a skeletal muscle fibre, the functional unit of contraction is the portion lying between:
options: One Z line and the next M line
questions.explanation:
NCERT defines the sarcomere as the portion of a myofibril between two successive Z lines. It is the functional unit of contraction.
The stretch between two M lines does not form a unit, because each M line lies in the middle of an A band.
Z line to M line is only half a sarcomere.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which pairs of human ribs are called floating ribs?
questions.explanation:
Humans have 12 pairs of ribs.
The last 2 pairs, the 11th and 12th, are not connected ventrally, so they are called floating ribs.
The 8th to 10th pairs are vertebrochondral (false) ribs, which join the seventh rib through hyaline cartilage.
The 1st to 7th pairs are true ribs.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (bones) with List-II (number in one limb):
List-I
(a) Carpals
(b) Tarsals
(c) Metacarpals
(d) Phalanges of fore limb
List-II
(i) 14
(ii) 5
(iii) 7
(iv) 8
questions.explanation:
(a) Carpals (wrist bones) = 8, so (a) matches (iv).
(b) Tarsals (ankle bones) = 7, so (b) matches (iii).
(c) Metacarpals (palm bones) = 5, so (c) matches (ii).
(d) Phalanges of each fore limb = 14, so (d) matches (i).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In an organised skeletal muscle, the muscle bundles (fascicles) are held together by a common layer called:
questions.explanation:
A skeletal muscle is made of many fascicles (muscle bundles).
These bundles are held together by a common layer of collagenous connective tissue called fascia.
Sarcolemma is the plasma membrane of a single muscle fibre, not a layer around bundles.
Sarcoplasmic reticulum is inside the fibre, and the synovial membrane belongs to joints.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The scapula is a large triangular flat bone located in the dorsal part of the thorax between the second and the seventh ribs.
Statement II: The two halves of the pelvic girdle meet ventrally to form the pubic symphysis, which contains hyaline cartilage.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The scapula is a large triangular flat bone in the dorsal thorax, between the 2nd and 7th ribs.
Statement II is incorrect. The pubic symphysis contains fibrous cartilage, not hyaline cartilage.
Hyaline cartilage is the type that connects the true ribs to the sternum.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The scapula lies on the dorsal side of the thorax between the second and seventh ribs. The glenoid cavity, located above its acromion, receives the head of the humerus.
Statement II: Each coxal bone forms by the fusion of the ilium, ischium and pubis. The acetabulum, present at the point of their fusion, receives the thigh bone.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. The scapula does lie dorsally between the 2nd and 7th ribs. However, the glenoid cavity lies below the acromion, not above it. The glenoid cavity articulates with the head of the humerus to form the shoulder joint.
Statement II is correct. Each coxal bone is formed by fusion of the ilium, ischium and pubis. The acetabulum at their point of fusion articulates with the femur.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following muscles show striations?
(i) Muscle moving the limb bones
(ii) Muscle of the heart wall
(iii) Muscle in the inner wall of the intestine
(iv) Muscle in the wall of the reproductive tract
(v) Muscles moving the tongue
questions.explanation:
(i) Striated: limb-moving muscles are skeletal muscles.
(ii) Striated: cardiac muscle is striated.
(iii) Not striated: the intestinal wall has visceral (smooth) muscle.
(iv) Not striated: the reproductive tract wall has visceral (smooth) muscle.
(v) Striated: the tongue is moved voluntarily by skeletal muscles.
So three of the five are striated.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (disorder) with List-II (feature):
List-I
(a) Myasthenia gravis
(b) Tetany
(c) Gout
(d) Osteoporosis
List-II
(i) Accumulation of uric acid crystals in joints
(ii) Decreased bone mass, often linked to low estrogen
(iii) Autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction
(iv) Rapid muscle spasms due to low $Ca^{++}$ in body fluid
questions.explanation:
(a) Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction, so (a)-(iii).
(b) Tetany is wild spasms caused by low $Ca^{++}$, so (b)-(iv).
(c) Gout is joint inflammation caused by uric acid crystals, so (c)-(i).
(d) Osteoporosis is an age-related loss of bone mass; a fall in estrogen is a common cause, so (d)-(ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Gout is an inflammation of joints caused by the accumulation of which of the following?
questions.explanation:
NCERT describes gout as inflammation of joints due to the accumulation of uric acid crystals.
Lactic acid builds up in muscles after repeated activation and causes fatigue, not gout.
Chondroitin salts make the cartilage matrix pliable. They do not cause joint disease.
Calcium carbonate deposits are not linked to gout in NCERT.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17 · Locomotion and Movement
